rv.q: However you classify 'The Moors' — comedy, drama, thriller satire, farce all apply at various times — there's no equivocating on its entertainment value.
It's a clever concept, but the execution of the play is erratic and the takeaways are sometimes unclear or too on the nose.

Kirsten Fitzgerald's deft direction, aided by Jeffrey Levin's brilliant sound design and K. Story's lighting, makes room for everything that Silverman's script has to throw at us: the mystery, the horror, the philosophy, the character depth, and the humor all play beautifully.

This wonderful production of Jen Silverman’s unconventional black comedy, beautifully directed with skill and flair, makes a fine show for returning to A Red Orchid Theatre, following months of a pandemic shutdown.

She is a Moor-Hen ( played to perfection by Dado). The sisters, Agatha ( as always, brilliantly brought to life by Karen Aldridge) and Hilday ( a wonderful comic touch by Christina Gorman). Agatha has her own agenda, believing that she is far better than anyone else and Hilday is tired of her sister, so she plans something special.

cn.t: Silverman's darkly comic feminist parody of Victorian drama earns praise for A Red Orchid's razor-sharp ensemble and clever absurdist subversion, though its slow build and surreal elements may not connect with all audiences.
